1: # Twyne pricing: new subscriptions
2: 
3: The new plan is `twyne_pro_v2`: USD 29/month before tax, with USD 10 in monthly retail Not Organic service credit. Unused included credit rolls over for one billing cycle. Top-ups are optional. Custom training and hosted voice are not part of this plan. BYOK and supported local writing remain available without this subscription.
4: 
5: The previous USD 12 Creem checkout is no longer the entry point for new sales. Existing Creem subscriptions, webhook handling, prices and entitlements are unchanged. The new plan is a hosted editorial AI wallet plan; it does not grant legacy Creem-only voice, research, collaboration or priority features.
6: 
7: ## Activation
8: 
9: New checkout is disabled by default. Before enabling:
10: 
11: 1. Deploy and map the provider plan `twyne_pro_v2` to the USD 29 monthly payment price and USD 10 grant; verify payment webhook and renewal/rollover behavior.
12: 2. Deploy the Not Organic `/v1/wallet` product-scoped `subscriptions` summary, which supplies plan, product, status and billing period timestamps in milliseconds.
13: 3. Verify linked account access, server-held assertion signing and `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` inference with actual wallet debits. Missing identity or token exchange errors must stop the hosted path instead of spending legacy server-provider funds.
14: 4. Set server `NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED=true` and build frontend with `PUBLIC_NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED=true`. Both gates must be enabled; unmapped provider checkout still rejects the purchase.
15: 5. Verify signed-in checkout and confirmed wallet status. A return URL never grants paid status. Check BYOK/local and existing Creem subscribers separately.
16: 
17: New subscription UI intentionally excludes legacy-only feature promises. Payment provider configuration and real purchase verification are deployment boundaries, not inferred from source tests.
18: 
19: ## One-time credit packs
20: 
21: Free accounts can buy `twyne_credit_10`, `twyne_credit_25` or `twyne_credit_50` through the same authenticated checkout action using `pack_id`, independently of Pro. No recurring payment or premium entitlement is created. Hosted editorial requests already use the linked account wallet without a Pro check; legacy voice, research and collaboration gates are unchanged.
22: 
23: Credit packs use the existing server `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` gate, independently of the Pro subscription flags. The pricing page also requires `checkout.available=true` and each pack in authenticated wallet `checkout.packIds`; it never enables an unmapped amount based on a UI constant. Keep the Pro gates disabled if only one-time purchases are ready.

119: /** Stable under reordering; changing a promise's wording makes it a new promise. */
120: export function promiseId(text: string): string {
121:   let hash = 2166136261;
122:   for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++)
123:     hash = Math.imul(hash ^ text.charCodeAt(i), 16777619);
124:   return `promise-${(hash >>> 0).toString(36)}-${text.length}`;
125: }

127: type ReadChoice = { value: string; review: boolean };
128: function record(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
129:   return !!value && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value);
130: }
131: function probability(value: unknown): value is number {
132:   return (
133:     typeof value === "number" &&
134:     Number.isFinite(value) &&
135:     value >= 0 &&
136:     value <= 1
137:   );
138: }
139: function readChoice(value: unknown, q: ChoiceQuestion): ReadChoice | undefined {
140:   if (
141:     !record(value) ||
142:     value.type !== "choice" ||
143:     typeof value.choice !== "string" ||
144:     !q.criteria.includes(value.choice) ||
145:     !probability(value.confidence) ||
146:     !record(value.probabilities)
147:   )
148:     return;
149:   const distribution = value.probabilities;
150:   if (
151:     Object.keys(distribution).length !== q.criteria.length ||
152:     !q.criteria.every((option) => probability(distribution[option]))
153:   )
154:     return;
155:   const probabilities = q.criteria.map(
156:     (option) => distribution[option] as number,
157:   );
158:   if (Math.abs(probabilities.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) - 1) > 0.02) return;
159:   const selected = distribution[value.choice] as number;
160:   if (selected + 0.0001 < Math.max(...probabilities)) return;
161:   const runnerUp = Math.max(
162:     0,
163:     ...q.criteria
164:       .filter((option) => option !== value.choice)
165:       .map((option) => distribution[option] as number),
166:   );
167:   // Product review gates, not claims about calibrated correctness.
168:   return {
169:     value: value.choice,
170:     review:
171:       value.confidence < 0.5 ||
172:       selected < 0.65 ||
173:       selected - runnerUp < 0.2 ||
174:       value.choice === INSUFFICIENT,
175:   };
176: }

187: export async function runWritingLens(

192:   const jobs: Job[] = [];

200:     id === "research" || (id === "scraps" && input.focus)
201:       ? input.draft.slice(0, MAX_DRAFT)
202:       : clip(input.draft, MAX_DRAFT, "Draft");
203:   const take = <T>(items: T[], label: string): T[] => {
204:     if (items.length > MAX_ITEMS)
205:       limits.add(`${label}: first ${MAX_ITEMS} of ${items.length}`);
206:     return items.slice(0, MAX_ITEMS);
207:   };
208:   const missing = (notice: string): WritingLensResult => ({
209:     status: "missing-input",

211:     coverage: "Nothing sent for review.",
212:     notice,
213:   });

218:   const audience = clip(

222:   );

233:       question,
234:       read(value) {

236:         if (!answer) return undefined;
237:         if (answer.value === NO_MATCH && !answer.review) return null;
238:         return {
239:           ...finding,
240:           title: answer.review
241:             ? `Review: ${answer.value.toLowerCase()}`
242:             : answer.value,
243:           detail: answer.review
244:             ? "The judgement is uncertain. Compare the quoted evidence before deciding."
245:             : details[answer.value] ||
246:               "Compare the supplied passages and decide whether this reading fits your intent.",
247:           needsReview: answer.review,
248:         };
249:       },
250:     };
251:   };

268:             "Reading `passage` using only `earlierText` and `audience`, which reader experience best fits? An intentional open question is different from a reference that cannot be understood. Do not assume any later explanation exists.",

282:             },
283:           ),
284:         },
285:       });
286:     });

295:     const dimensions = [

139:   const link = await ctx.runQuery(linkedDidReference, {
140:     productSubject: identity.subject || identity.tokenIdentifier,
141:   });
142:   if (!link) return { ok: false, error: "account not linked" };
143: 
144:   try {
145:     const token = await issueNotOrganicAccessToken({
146:       did: link.did,
147:       feature: JUDGEMENT_FEATURE,
148:       capabilities: [JUDGEMENT_CAPABILITY],
149:       sessionVersion: link.sessionVersion,
150:     });
151:     const result = await providerJsonRequest<JudgementResponse>(
152:       JUDGEMENT_PATH,
153:       token,
154:       {
155:         method: "POST",
156:         signal: AbortSignal.timeout(40_000),
157:         body: JSON.stringify(body),
158:         // The gateway reserves credit before calling upstream, so it needs a
159:         // key to settle against. A fresh one per attempt is deliberate: each
160:         // ask is a new judgement the writer asked for, and deduplicating on
161:         // content would silently return a stale grade for an edited draft.
162:         headers: { "idempotency-key": crypto.randomUUID() },
163:       },
164:       { issuer: notOrganicIssuer(), feature: JUDGEMENT_FEATURE },
165:     );
166:     return { ok: true, body: result };
167:   } catch (error) {
168:     // `providerJsonRequest` puts the upstream status in its message. Map the
169:     // ones a caller can act on and swallow the rest — the detail can echo the
170:     // request, which here is the writer's own draft.
171:     const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "";
172:     if (message.includes("(429)")) return { ok: false, error: "rate limited" };
173:     if (message.includes("(529)")) return { ok: false, error: "overloaded" };
174:     if (message.includes("(401)") || message.includes("(403)")) {
175:       return { ok: false, error: "unauthorized" };
176:     }
177:     if (message.includes("(402)")) return { ok: false, error: "no credit" };
178:     if (message.includes("(404)")) {
179:       // The gateway has not shipped `/v1/judgement` yet.
180:       return { ok: false, error: "unsupported" };
181:     }
182:     if (message.includes("(422)")) return { ok: false, error: "malformed" };
183:     return { ok: false, error: "provider" };
184:   }
185: }

188: async function askDirect(
189:   key: string,
190:   body: Record<string, unknown>,
191: ): Promise<
192:   { ok: true; body: JudgementResponse } | { ok: false; error: string }
193: > {
194:   let res: Response;
195:   try {
196:     res = await fetch(DIRECT_ENDPOINT, {
197:       method: "POST",
198:       signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000),
199:       headers: {
200:         "Content-Type": "application/json",
201:         Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`,
202:       },
203:       body: JSON.stringify(body),
204:     });
205:   } catch {
206:     return { ok: false, error: "network" };
207:   }
208:   if (!res.ok) {
209:     // 429 and 529 are both "try again shortly"; the caller decides whether a
210:     // background pass is worth retrying at all. Never surface the body, which
211:     // can echo the request.
212:     const kind =
213:       res.status === 429
214:         ? "rate limited"
215:         : res.status === 529
216:           ? "overloaded"
217:           : res.status === 401
218:             ? "unauthorized"
219:             : res.status === 422
220:               ? "malformed"
221:               : `http ${res.status}`;
222:     return { ok: false, error: kind };
223:   }
224:   try {
225:     return { ok: true, body: (await res.json()) as JudgementResponse };
226:   } catch {
227:     return { ok: false, error: "provider" };
228:   }
229: }

1: /**
2:  * TypeSafe "System One" (Jev) — typed questions and answers.
3:  *
4:  * Jev does not generate text. It answers a fixed set of questions about some
5:  * state, and returns a calibrated probability distribution for each one. That
6:  * is the whole surface: three question kinds, three answer shapes.
7:  *
8:  *   Noul    probability of yes, 0..1
9:  *   Choice  pick one option, plus the probability of every option
10:  *   Score   ordered levels, returning a probability-weighted value
11:  *
12:  * This module is transport-free on purpose. It builds requests and reads
13:  * answers; `convex/systemOne.ts` is the only place that holds the API key and
14:  * talks to the network, because the key must never reach the browser bundle.
15:  *
16:  * Costs, measured against the live API rather than quoted from the docs: the
17:  * full 11-criterion rubric spine batched into one request took 378 ms and
18:  * 1,401 input tokens — $0.0000588, or roughly 17,000 rubric passes per dollar.
19:  * Output tokens are free. This is cheap enough to run on a typing pause.

No — `WritingTools` has no Storybook story.

* 11 `*.stories.tsx` exist (brief card, UI primitives, editor outline/table, etc.), none under `src/components/writing-tools/`.
* It's only wired as a full route:
  * `src/routes/writing-tools/index.tsx` → `<WritingTools />`
  * Linked from desk menu in `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1109` (`/writing-tools/` — "Explore revisions, voice, and evidence")
  * Component: `src/components/writing-tools/writing-tools.tsx` (827 lines, Qwik `component$`, browser-only)

What it does — 8 read-only "lenses" defined in `src/utils/writing-lenses.ts:WRITING_LENSES`:

1. `reader` — Read without the ending
2. `revision` — What did the edit cost? (before/after across 5 dimensions)
3. `voice` — Protect your voice (vs saved voice samples)
4. `promises` — Promises to the reader (setup → payoff)
5. `scraps` — Give scraps another life
6. `room` — Make disagreement useful (persona-note pairs)
7. `circling` — Are these edits moving? (last 4 snapshots)
8. `research` — Check research drift (claim vs supplied source excerpt)

Flow: loads active folio draft + revisions + room notes from IDB (`loadFolioContentFromIdb`, `loadRevisionHistory`, `loadPersonaNotesLocally`), plus per-folio notebook from `writing-tools-storage.ts` (`writing-tools:${folioId}` → audience, voiceSamples, scraps, sources, intentionalPromises, local IDB only). `runWritingLens()` builds System One `choice`/`noul` jobs and calls `api.systemOne.ask` via Convex (`convex/systemOne.ts` → Not Organic `/v1/judgement`, Jev). Quotes only from supplied evidence, never edits the draft.

content.text:
Batch 2 done — 11 new story files, build passes, typecheck shows only the pre-existing `note-gate` error. Coverage went from 12 → 32 components:

* **Editor**: `InsertPanels` (diagram modal with the new side-by-side preview, footnote/endnote, image bar + error states), `SlashCommandMenu` (all/filtered/no-match/closed), `ImageInspector` (ready/uploading/failed/disabled)
* **Desk**: `ChartTable`, `DailyActivityChart`, `TokenDimensions` (+no-coverage), `UsageBreakdowns` (feature/provider), `WritingActivity` — sharing one `story-fixtures.ts` for metrics/tokens
* **Onboarding**: `WritingFormatInput` · **UI**: `SearchableModelSelect` · **Landing**: `WorkspacePreview`

Still uncovered are mostly provider-bound pieces (`ChatComposer`, `SpeakButton`, `VoiceRecorder`, `SyncIndicator`, `CommentsPanel`, `FolioMenu`, `PersonasPanel`, `RubricPanel`, `ManuscriptPanel`, `TwyneEditor`, auth/blog/legal pages). Those need Convex/auth/router scaffolding in Storybook — say the word and I'll do a batch 3 with lightweight mocked providers.

content.text:
Both done and visually verified in headless Chromium (122 stories indexed, zero page errors):

**Editor-like diagram preview**
* New `editor/mermaid-theme.ts` — one shared config (base theme, ink lines, serif labels, newsprint node fills). The manuscript renderer and the insert-dialog preview both use it, so they can't drift apart. Editor gating keeps the first paint themed.
* The modal preview now sits on manuscript paper (`--color-paper`, ink serif context) with the SVG centered and scaled — I confirmed the side-by-side render: source left, themed flowchart right.

**Landing plates (photos → live UI previews)**
* New `landing/plate-previews.tsx` — four static, provider-free components: `BriefPlatePreview` (real `DossierPreview` with canned data), `DraftPlatePreview` (manuscript page, including the strike-and-correct gesture), `NotesPlatePreview` (margin marks + Skeptic/Gentle Reader cards + real `GradeStamp`), `SourcesPlatePreview` (apparatus records with verified/needs-review states). All `aria-hidden`, since the step copy carries the meaning — same pattern as the hero photo.
* `landing-page.tsx` renders them inside the existing tilted plate frames; the four `product-*-v2` photo references are gone. Hero and closing photos untouched.
* New `Landing/PlatePreviews` stories (brief/draft/notes/sources) — screenshots confirm they look authentically Twyne.

Typecheck is clean apart from the pre-existing `note-gate` failure, and `storybook.build` passes. One note: the old plate `.webp` files are still on disk under `public/assets/landing/` — say the word if you want them deleted.

content.text:
Both fixes are in. Honest report on what I found:

**Ctrl+A** — I verified headlessly (continuous *and* paginated) that with focus in the manuscript, Ctrl+A already selects exactly the document. The page-wide selection happens when the keypress never reaches the editor — focus on a widget, or a field like the math source textarea where ProseMirror was *stealing* Ctrl+A to select the whole doc. New capture-phase handler on the editor mount (`twyne-editor.tsx`) makes it deterministic: Mod-A anywhere in the manuscript selects the whole manuscript and nothing more; inside a text field it keeps native field selection. Verified headless — anchor and focus both stay inside the document.

**Autoscroll / empty space** — I could *not* reproduce a caret escaping the viewport in a fresh folio: the scroll containers followed 30–40 paragraphs of typing in both modes. What I did find and fix: the sticky colophon bar at the manuscript's bottom edge can cover the current line with zero margin — both manuscript scrollers now have `scroll-pb-12` so programmatic scrolls always leave 3rem of breathing room.

Two things I need from you to close the autoscroll half, since it must be state I didn't hit:
1. Paginated sheets or continuous column when it happens — and does the caret drop *below* the visible area, or does typed text get *replaced/lost*?
2. Solo folio or shared (Lix/collab) doc — and roughly how long is the manuscript?

If it's reproducible on your machine, the fastest path is you reproducing it once while I watch the scroll offsets — or just tell me the above and I'll dig in that configuration.
